title: Polish
shortDescription: Self-hosted UI review for code and copy
description: polish reviews UI code, interface writing, and accessibility, and returns a weighted 0-100 score with severity, category, exact file and line, plus a concrete fix. Self-hosted CLI and MCP server, your own API key, no bots in your repo, no quotas.

details.heading: Why It Exists
details.text: Design feedback usually arrives after a screen ships, during a review call, or not at all. polish moves that review into the codebase: it reads the UI files you touched and returns findings before merge. No design handoff, no review queue, no waiting for someone to be free.

details.heading: What It Checks
details.text: polish reviews React, Vue, Svelte, and CSS files against a layered rubric: usability heuristics, design craft (typography, color, spacing, motion, components, writing), and accessibility (contrast, keyboard support, semantics, touch targets, reduced motion). The craft layer also covers interface writing: headings, descriptions, labels, helper text, and common AI-writing signals like filler words and padded conclusions. All three layers are on by default, and you can switch any of them off to cut token cost on large reviews.

details.heading: How Scoring Works
details.text: Each run returns a weighted 0-100 score. Critical findings deduct 22, serious findings deduct 9, and moderate findings deduct 3. There is no severity ceiling. On a real run, the demo card scored 62 before the fix and 78 after, and the same file can score a few points differently across models. Treat any single number as a signal, not a grade.

details.heading: Install and Run
details.text: Clone the repo, link the command once, and set one API key. git clone https://github.com/tomiabe/polish, run npm link inside it, then export GROQ_API_KEY (or OPENAI, ANTHROPIC, GEMINI, or OPENROUTER) in your shell profile. You can also set a fallback chain in your config so polish tries multiple providers in order until one succeeds. From there, polish audits the files matched by your config, or the specific paths you pass it.

details.heading: Built for Teams and Agents
details.text: The same review engine runs as a CLI for developers and an MCP server for AI agents inside a project, so both get identical results. Every run emits a machine-readable receipt with polishApplied: true, a run ID, score, and files reviewed. Verify mode re-checks only previous findings after you fix them, returning a fresh score and receipt at a fraction of the cost of a full review. Run polish init-agent to write AGENTS.md into your repo, giving coding agents a repeatable review loop: run Polish, read the receipt, apply fixes, then verify. polish exits with code 1 when critical findings exist, so it works as a pre-commit or CI gate. The rubric is plain data, so you can swap in your own design philosophy without rewriting the tool.
